svg.title: RIEMANN R3 — From prime sums to the zero-free half-plane: the analytic half of the proof, lemma by lemma
svg.desc: The chapter proves one theorem: if families of definite unitary groups carry slope data, and auxiliary CM fields exist at every scale of long windows, then no primitive Dirichlet L-function vanishes right of the critical line. Its blueprint chapter has five sections and 24 statements, and every one is a card here: the Lean declaration, the statement, the proof and what it uses. Read it from the foot up: the theorem is at the bottom, its two inputs stand on either side, and each column above is one strand of the argument. An arrow from A to B says that the proof of B uses A; a dashed arrow says that B takes A as a hypothesis, which the proof text names and the uses list does not. The blueprint says of this chapter that the square root in the core inequality is the Riemann Hypothesis. No Lean was built: see diagram R1, band 5.
svg.text: RIEMANN · R3

text.tspan: The chapter, from its definitions down to its theorem

svg.text: Top row: the five definitions the chapter is written in. Left column: Landau's theorem, then the auxiliary fields. Second column: the core inequality. The top row of results and the right half: the local link at inert primes, from a mean value theorem for bad shares up to the lattice-gain bound, and slope data from it. Nothing is used before it is proved.

def ZeroFreeAll : Prop := ZeroFreeOn fun _ => True
We say that primitive L-functions do not vanish right of the critical line if L(ψ, s) ≠ 0 for every
primitive Dirichlet character ψ and every s with Re s > 1/2. For the trivial character L(ψ, s)
= ζ(s), and at s = 1 we use the conventional value ζ(1) = (γ - log 4π)/2, which is not
zero.

text.tspan: Classes of families with slope data

svg.text: def TopG : Prop :=
∀ (la : ℝ) (G : FReq), 1 < la → HostExW la G.req →
(∀ {eps : ℝ} (Fm : FamP eps), G.cls la Fm → HypV Fm.toFamCore)
→ FamilyClassConnected (G.cls la)
We say that families have slope data if, for every λ > 1 and every requirement on auxiliary
fields, the following holds. Suppose fields meeting the requirement exist on windows [Y, Y^λ],
and the members of every family(@def-family) in the corresponding class eventually satisfy
the Tate–Shafarevich bound. Then for some constants e_D, e_L and every small ε, some
family in the class carries slope data (def-slope-data) at every large x of its windows.

text.tspan: A mean value theorem for bad shares

svg.text: def TheoremMV7 : Prop :=
∀ (p : ℕ) [Fact p.Prime] (s r : ℕ) [NeZero r] (LL : Letters (2 *
s + 1)) (T : TieData)
(a E : ℝ) (Yl n₀ dd : Fin T.t → ℕ) (ρ : Fin r),
p ≠ 2 → 2 ≤ r → (ρ : ℕ) = r - 1 → T.Admissible LL →
ChainOrderLetters LL → ConditionShape s T →
1 ≤ a → 1 ≤ E → (∀ i, 1 ≤ Yl i ∧ 0 < dd i ∧ IsCoprime (dd i :
ℤ) p) →
… 23 more lines
Mean value theorem. Let p be an odd prime, r ≥ 2, and consider lattices Y(n) of polynomials
with the Fock pairing attached to a system of letters with ties n = (n_i) in the chain order. Let
1 ≤ a, 1 ≤ E, and for each tie i let n_i run over an arithmetic progression n_(0,i) + d_i j,
0 ≤ j < Y_i, with d_i prime to p; let P be the product of these progressions. Under the size
hypothesis, (1)/(|P|)sum_(n ∈ P)bad_D (Y(n) ) ≤ sum_i varepsilon_i, where bad_D
is the number of bad vectors at depth D = ⌊ t(E + κ) + κ⌋ and varepsilon_i is an explicit
function of the tie size, Y_i and κ.
We have not checked the details. The mean value theorem is proved by following invariant
factors along the progressions: as n_i moves along its progression, the elementary divisors of
the Fock Gram matrix change in a controlled way, so a vector can be bad for only a bounded
proportion of the steps.
Stated with no other statement
Proof uses nothing the blueprint names

admitted local datum satisfies the bound on the dimensions of the base blocks, the two bounds
on positive parts, and the bound on directions. Then there is a constant C_M ≥ 0 such that

the block bound for dual families, and the bound on block sums of prop-block-sums-ranges.
Take C_M from prop-block-sums-ranges, which gives the bound on block sums. The block
bound for dual families follows from the valuation of blocks over Z_p, and the bounds on

text.tspan: The local estimate at inert primes

svg.text: theorem loc_proved : Loc
Every member D of a family satisfies the local estimate at inert primes in closed form: for all
constants for which D is admitted, there is C_0 such that for C ≥ C_0 the following holds. Let p
≥ 13 be a prime, mathcal O' / mathcal O an unramified quadratic extension of discrete
valuation rings of residue characteristic p attached to D, and let the orbit data (T, r, L_1,
L_2), weights lambda_0 and scale parameters a, Y satisfy the explicit size conditions (among
them 256(m+1)^2|T|Y^2 ≤ p^(L_1 - 1) and an upper bound for a in terms of C, p and the
orbit data). …
The proof reduces the estimate in four steps to statements about the polynomials of the local
construction, each proved directly.
Membership. A Gram-matrix estimate holds for every member with the explicit constants 26,
2, 24, 60: it follows from a choice of test vectors, the membership of their images and a
numerical bound. …
Three steps. The membership condition follows from the operator step (applying a derivation
∂/∂ x, a multiplication by x, or their product keeps the polynomials within the bounds for their
degrees and valuations), the plane bound below, and the arithmetic step. …
Plane bound. Consider polynomials A_i over a discrete valuation ring of residue characteristic
p, supported on the variables attached to the letters of a valid system of frames of rank r, with
signed chain data tied to the frames. …
… and 1 more paragraphs in the blueprint's proof.

def FormB : Prop := ∀ la : ℝ, 1 < la → Λ.FormBAt la
Let λ > 1 and 0 < θ < 1. If for arbitrarily large Y G_m(x) ≤ x^θ for all x ∈ [Y, Y^λ],
then L(χ, s) ≠ 0 for every χ ∈ ⟨ψ⟩ and every s with Re s > θ. The argument is Landau's
theorem on Dirichlet series with non-negative coefficients. The bound is assumed only on the
windows [Y, Y^λ], not for all large x.
Landau's theorem on Dirichlet series with non-negative coefficients. The Mellin transform of
G_m is a combination of -(L')/(L)(s,χ) divided by s(s-1). A zero of some L(χ, s) with Re
s > θ would give it a pole. …

text.tspan: Served twists bound the sums over primes

svg.text: theorem closed_servF_of_servT_of_dGamSize {𝒞 : FamClass} (sel :
_root_.Formalism.L2.TwistSelection 𝒞) (hD : Closed 𝒞 fun Fm _
=> DGamSize Fm) (h :
_root_.Formalism.L2.G.ServT.SelectionServed 𝒞 sel) :
Closed 𝒞 fun Fm _ => WeilJacquetShalikaLaw.ServF Fm
Each lattice u of a member of a family carries a positive integer D(u); we read it as a
discriminant. Say the member satisfies the size bound if log D(u) ≤ C f Nlog(fN) for all u,
with f and N the size parameters of the family. Let mathcal C be a class of families with a
choice of twists that is served (as in thm-twisted-admissibility), and suppose that the
members of its families eventually satisfy the size bound. Then they eventually satisfy the
bound for sums over primes that the comparison between twisted and untwisted members
requires. …
A served choice of twists supplies the two hypotheses of the general bound for sums over
primes: the twisted comparison at each member, and the conditions on the kernels of the
twists from the point where the choice is made. The size bound is the remaining hypothesis.

text.tspan: Large sets without short linear relations

svg.text: theorem hostThickExists : HostThickExists
There is C > 0 such that for all n ≥ 1 and L ≥ 2 there is a set T of integers 0 ≤ s < n/4L
with |T| ≥ (n)/(L) e^-Csqrtlog n log L, such that no three distinct s_1, s_2, s_3 ∈
T satisfy j(s_2 - s_1) = i(s_3 - s_1) with 0 < |i|, |j| ≤ L and i ≠ j. Consequently,
in a cyclic group generated by an element a of order n, the translates u_0 + Ta meet every
arithmetic progression t, t + h, …, t + (L-1)h in at most two points when h has order
greater than 4L, and every coset t + ⟨ h⟩ in at most one point when h has order at most 4L.
Write integers in base B with S digits, each digit small compared with B/L, and keep those

data (def-connected-families), and that auxiliary CM fields with the properties of

arguments. The blueprint's uses list for the proof names neither, so no solid arrow joins them.

both hypotheses is thm-zero-free-from-families in the outline chapter (diagram R1,
band 3), which cites all three.

text.tspan: Zero-freeness from slope data and auxiliary fields

svg.text: theorem zeroFreeAll_of_topG {la : ℝ} (hla : 1 < la) (h : TopG) (hS : ∀ ψ : PChar, HostExW la (GChi ψ).req) : ZeroFreeAll
Let λ > 1. Suppose that families have slope data (def-connected-families), and
Fix a primitive ψ and a small ε > 0.

Slope data. The fields of hypothesis 2 satisfy the Tate–Shafarevich bound, so the members of every family built on them satisfy it too. Hypothesis 1 then gives constants e_D, e_L, independent of ε, and a family built on these fields that carries slope data (def-slope-data) at every large x of its windows.
The core inequality. At each such x, thm-core-inequality gives G_m(x) ≤ x^(1/2 + (e_D + e_L + 7)ε).
Landau's theorem. These are bounds on windows [Y, Y^λ] of arbitrarily large Y, with c = e_D + e_L + 7 independent of ε, so thm-zero-free-from-windows applies.
… and 1 more paragraphs in the blueprint's proof.

text.tspan: The argument in the chapter's own words, section by section

svg.text: The first paragraph of each section's introduction in the blueprint, in the chapter's order, with the statements each section holds. Abridged where marked with ….
This section reduces zero-freeness to an upper bound on windows. The weighted Chebyshev
function G_m (def-chebyshev-weighted) combines the von Mangoldt sums of the characters
in ⟨ψ⟩, with weights that make its Dirichlet coefficients non-negative. Landau's theorem then
shows that a bound G_m(x) ≤ x^θ on windows [Y, Y^λ] of arbitrarily large Y excludes zeros
with Re s > θ (thm-zero-free-from-windows).
Holds def-chebyshev-weighted, def-zero-free-primitive, thm-landau-windows,
For each primitive ψ and each scale x of a window we need an abelian CM field E: the families
live over it, and the prime sums run over its Frobenius classes. thm-auxiliary-fields
builds it from the Tate–Shafarevich bound, with Galois group {pm1}^2 × A, degree about
x^(2+8ε), and |L'/L(1,χ)| ≤ Clog x for the characters that matter. For the real
characters we do not prove this bound one character at a time: we choose the auxiliary
primes q and d outside a small exceptional set, which a mean-square estimate controls (
lem-good-auxiliary-primes).
Holds def-auxiliary-field-data, lem-good-auxiliary-primes,
This section proves the bound that Landau's theorem needs at every scale x where slope
data exist: G_m(x) ≤ x^(1/2 + (e_D + e_L + 7)ε) (thm-core-inequality). Each
member of a family has a gap, the excess of its von Mangoldt sums over the primes inert in E
above their main terms. Orthogonality of the characters of Gal(E/ℚ) turns the sum of the
gaps into twisted von Mangoldt sums, among them G_m(x) (thm-chain-averaging). The
slope inequality bounds each gap (thm-member-gap-bound); we read it as Bost's slope
inequality for hermitian lattices, used as an arithmetic form of Stepanov's method.
Holds def-slope-data, thm-chain-averaging, thm-core-inequality,
The core inequality assumes slope data. This section derives them from the family
hypotheses of chap-families (thm-families-connected), by a sequence of comparisons
that we have not unfolded. Two of its inputs are stated here: twisted admissibility, by which a
suitable choice of twists gives the second admissibility condition (
thm-twisted-admissibility), and large sets of twists without short linear relations, built as
Behrend built sets without three-term progressions (lem-behrend-sets). A third input, the
local link at inert primes, has its own section (sec-zf-local-link).
Holds def-connected-families, lem-behrend-sets, lem-served-twists-prime-sums,
thm-families-connected, thm-twisted-admissibility

text.tspan: 5. The local link at inert primes

svg.text: This section proves the local inequality behind the slope inequality: at each prime inert in the
auxiliary field, the von Mangoldt class sums of a member are bounded by the gains of its theta
lifts (thm-prime-sums-lattice-gains). thm-families-connected uses it. The proof
combines three theorems about lattices of polynomials over an unramified quadratic extension
of discrete valuation rings: the local estimate at inert primes (
thm-local-estimate-inert-primes), a bound on the mean bad share of Fock lattices (
thm-fock-bad-share-mean), and a large direct summand of low degree (
thm-large-summand-low-degree).
Holds prop-block-bounds-from-four, prop-block-sums-ranges,
thm-fock-bad-share-mean, thm-large-summand-low-degree,
thm-local-estimate-inert-primes, thm-mean-value-bad-shares,
23 statements in the five sections, and 1 at the chapter's root: thm-zero-free-from-connected.
